title: NodeKit capability contract v1
$comment: A falsifiable bet, written BEFORE a capability is built. The question this exists to force is 'what will we measure that this helps with, and what result would make us delete it?' — asked before the build, when the answer is a prediction, rather than after, when it is a defence. declaredAt must precede the measurement it is judged against; a contract written afterwards is a discussion, not a bet, and the gate refuses it.

capability.$comment: The thing being proposed. One capability per contract; a contract covering two is two bets nobody can settle separately.

declaredAt.$comment: When the bet was placed. Load-bearing: the gate compares this against the measurement's observedAt and refuses a contract that postdates its own evidence.

questionItServes.$comment: A question a USER asks, in their words. Not a capability restated as a question. 'Which sponsors also work on what X works on?' is one; 'can we traverse the graph?' is the capability wearing a question mark.

whyExistingToolsCannot.$comment: Why the tools already in the system cannot answer it. If this is hard to write, that is the finding.

baseline.$comment: What the metric reads WITHOUT the capability, measured rather than assumed. A baseline nobody measured makes every later comparison unfalsifiable.

howMeasured.$comment: The command or procedure that produces this number, so the same instrument reads the baseline and the result. Two instruments is how a capability wins on paper.

killCondition.$comment: Structured, not prose. Prose kill conditions are argued with; thresholds are evaluated. ANY clause triggering means the capability is killed. Empty is forbidden — a bet with no losing outcome is not a bet.

comparator.$comment: Read as: kill if the observed value is <comparator> <value>.

consumers.$comment: What will CALL this capability once built, named specifically. A capability whose only consumer is itself — padding its own output, enriching a list nobody asked to be enriched — is decorative by definition, and the gate says so regardless of how well it measures. Empty is allowed and is an immediate decorative verdict, which is the honest state for a capability built before anything wanted it.

kind.$comment: user-facing means a person can ask for it. internal-only is the padding case: real, but not a reason to keep a capability alive on its own.

decoupledFrom.$comment: When a capability decision is entangled with an infrastructure decision, name the confound and say whether it can be removed before deciding either. Choosing a capability while its hosting cost is still in the comparison answers the wrong question.

adoptionDecision.$comment: If the capability is a dependency rather than code. fractionUsed is the field that catches adopting a framework for a tenth of it, and inheritedCosts is what that tenth drags in.
